A.explanation: There is no horizontal force when air resistance is ignored, so there is no horizontal deceleration.

B.explanation: There is no horizontal deceleration and vertical acceleration does not change because weight is constant.

C.explanation: No horizontal force gives constant horizontal velocity, while constant weight gives constant acceleration $g$ downwards vertically.

D.explanation: Horizontal motion is constant velocity, but vertical acceleration stays constant downwards and does not decrease then increase.

hints: Notice the parabolic path and the phrase when air resistance is ignored, so only weight acts on the golf ball after launch.
Connect force to acceleration separately for each component: zero horizontal force means zero horizontal acceleration, while constant vertical weight means constant vertical acceleration.
Check which horizontal description means zero acceleration and which vertical description means uniform $g$ downwards through the upward and downward parts of flight.
walkthrough: Identify the motion from the diagram as projectile motion with the symmetric curved path, and use the condition that air resistance is ignored.
State the forces: horizontally there is no force, vertically the only force is weight $W = mg$ acting downwards and constant in magnitude.
Apply $F = ma$ to the horizontal component: $F_x = 0$ so $a_x = 0$, therefore horizontal velocity $v_x$ does not change and remains constant velocity.
Apply $F = ma$ to the vertical component: $F_y = mg$ downwards so $a_y = g$ constant downwards, about $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Interpret the effect: constant downward acceleration makes upward vertical velocity decrease to zero at the top and then downward speed increase, but the acceleration itself stays constant.
Match constant velocity horizontally with constant acceleration downwards vertically. This is option C.
